newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow drives Australian stocks down at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow drives Australian stocks down at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened lower on Thursday, the market driven down by a weaker Wall Street beset by interest rate concerns.
The All Ordinaries index lost nine points to 2,445.4.
Brokers said there had been little to engender confidence from offshore market closes with local February jobs data due later today further eroding early interest.
"It's not going anywhere so far," said a a Sydney broker, adding that some traders may be waiting to see the impact of February employment data due at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
"I'm not expecting anything from the jobs numbers but it may push things around a bit."

Results continued with Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer rising five cents to A$5.96 (US$4.71) after its sharply higher first half net profit of A$273.6 million and forecasts of similar profit growth in the second half.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to five, while 46 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
